The wooden A-frame structure was inspired by {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|en|Shimane Prefecture|qid=Q132751|lt=Shimane Prefecture}}'s classical Japanese shrine [[Izumo-taisha]]. It was designed by architect {{ill|Hego Fuchino|qid=Q58471955|lt=Hego Fuchino}} and built by master carpenter [[Ichisaburo Takata]].

The primary ''[[kami]]'' of this shrine is [[Ōkuninushi]] and Hawaii [[Ubusunagami|Ubusuna]]-no-{{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Kami}}. The shrine is the site of the annual New Year's Day ''{{ill|Hatsumōde|ar|هاتسوموده|de|Hatsumōde|es|Hatsumōde|eu|Hatsumōde|fa|هاتسوموده|fr|Hatsumōde|hu|Hacumóde|hy|Հացումոդե|id|Hatsumōde|ja|初詣|jv|Hatsumōde|ko|하쓰모데|my|ဟဆုမိုဒဲ|pl|Hatsumōde|pt|Hatsumōde|ru|Хацумодэ|simple|Hatsumoude|tr|Hatsumōde|zh|初詣|zh_classical|初詣|qid=Q1032381|lt=Hatsumōde}}'' as well as other events throughout the year. A replica of the [[Hiroshima Peace Bell]] is on view. ==History==
Hawaii Izumo Taisha was founded in 1906 when Rev. Katsuyoshi Miyao opened a temporary {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=worship site}} on Aala Street near Aala Park on 26 September 1906.<ref>Maeda, Takakazu. Hawaii no Jinjashi. Taimeido. Tokyo. 1999. p. 153.</ref> A temporary shrine building was completed on 25 August 1907. A permanent [[honden|shrine building]] was completed in 1922.<ref>Maeda, Takakazu. Hawaii no Jinjashi. Taimeido. Tokyo. 1999. p. 161.</ref> By 1941, there were branches of Izumo Taishakyo operating in {{ill|Hilo, Hawaii|en|Hilo, Hawaii|qid=Q216258|lt=Hilo}}, {{ill|Wailuku, Hawaii|en|Wailuku, Hawaii|qid=Q2087831|lt=Wailuku}}, {{ill|Waipahu, Hawaii|en|Waipahu, Hawaii|qid=Q637246|lt=Waipahu}}, {{ill|Pearl City, Hawaii|en|Pearl City, Hawaii|qid=Q572052|lt=Pearl City}}, [[:en:Honouliuli|Honouliuli]], Ewa Lower Camp, [[:en:Aiea, Hawaii|Aiea]], and [[:en:Kakaako, Hawaii|Kakaako]].<ref>Maeda, Takakazu. Hawaii no Jinjashi. Taimeido. Tokyo. 1999. p. 174.</ref>

The shrine was closed on 7 December 1941 at the outset of {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|qid=Q184425|lt=Pacific War}}. The shrine was illegally acquired by the {{ill|Honolulu County, Hawaii|af|Honolulu County|ar|مقاطعة هونولولو (هاواي)|azb|هونولولو بؤلگه‌سی، هاوایی|bar|City and County of Honolulu, Hawaii|bg|Хонолулу (окръг)|bpy|হনলুলু কাউন্টি, হাৱাই|ce|Гонолулу (гуо, Гавай)|ceb|Honolulu County|cy|Honolulu County, Hawaii|da|Honolulu County|de|City and County of Honolulu|es|Condado de Honolulu|eu|Honolulu konderria|fa|شهر و شهرستان هونولولو|fi|Honolulun piirikunta|fr|Comté d'Honolulu|frr|Honolulu County|ga|Contae Honolulu, Hawaii|glk|هؤنؤلۊلۊ شأرستان (هاوايي)|he|מחוז הונולולו|hu|Honolulu megye|hy|Հոնոլուլու շրջան (Հավայի)|id|County Honolulu, Hawaii|ilo|Kondado ti Honolulu, Hawaii|it|Contea di Honolulu|ja|ホノルル郡 (ハワイ州)|ko|호놀룰루군|la|Honolulu Comitatus|mzn|هونولولو شهرستان (هاوایی)|nds|Honolulu County|nl|Honolulu County|no|Honolulu County|pl|Hrabstwo Honolulu|pnb|ہونولولو کاؤنٹی|pt|Condado de Honolulu|ru|Гонолулу (округ)|sh|Honolulu County, Hawaii|simple|Honolulu County, Hawaii|sq|Honolulu County|sr|Округ Хонолулу (Хаваји)|sv|Honolulu County|tr|Honolulu County|tt|Гонолулу (округ, Гавай)|uk|Гонолулу (округ, Гаваї)|ur|ہونولولو کاؤنٹی، ہوائی|war|Condado han Honolulu, Hawaii|zh|檀香山市縣|zh_min_nan|Honolulu Kūn (Hawaii)|qid=Q487704|lt=City and County of Honolulu}} in June 1942. After {{ill|Internment of Japanese Americans|ar|اعتقال الأمريكيين اليابانيين|be|Інтэрніраванне японцаў у ЗША|ca|Camps de concentració per als japonesos americans|cs|Internace Američanů japonského původu|de|Internierung japanischstämmiger Amerikaner|el|Εγκλεισμός των Ιαπώνων Αμερικανών|es|Campos de internamiento para japoneses en los Estados Unidos|fa|بازداشت دسته‌جمعی ژاپنی آمریکایی‌ها|fi|Amerikanjapanilaisten internointi|fr|Internement des Nippo-Américains|he|כליאת היפנים בארצות הברית|id|Penginterniran orang Jepang-Amerika|it|Internamento dei giapponesi negli Stati Uniti|ja|日系人の強制収容|ko|일본계 미국인의 강제수용|ms|Penahanan warga bangsa Jepun di Amerika Syarikat|nl|Internering van Japanse Amerikanen|no|Internering av japansk-amerikanere under andre verdenskrig|pl|Internowanie Amerykanów pochodzenia japońskiego w czasie II wojny światowej|ps|د جاپاني امریکایانو بندي کول|pt|Campos de internamento de nipo-americanos|ru|Интернирование японцев в США|simple|Japanese American internment|sv|Internering av japaner i USA under andra världskriget|th|การกักกันชาวอเมริกันเชื้อสายญี่ปุ่น|tr|ABD vatandaşı Japonların enterne edilmesi|zh|對日裔美國人的囚禁|qid=Q936604|lt=internment}} on the mainland, the priest and family returned to Hawaii in mid-December 1945. A temporary shrine was consecrated in a residence-like warehouse in McCully area of Honolulu and served as a {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=worship site}} from 1946-1968.<ref>Miyao, Richard T. Izumo Taishakyo Mission of Hawaii Centennial Anniversary Saga of a Church in Hawaii, 1906-2006. Hawaii Hochi, Ltd. Honolulu, Hawaii. 2006. p. 87-88.</ref>

The original shrine property was returned to the shrine organization in October 1961 as a result of lengthy legal and legislative appeals.<ref>Maeda, Takakazu. Hawaii no Jinjashi. Taimeido. Tokyo. 1999. p. 180.</ref> The shrine building was moved in 1963 to its present location to make way for {{ill|Federal Housing Administration|ar|إدارة الإسكان الفيدرالية|de|Federal Housing Administration|es|Administración Federal de Vivienda|fr|Federal Housing Administration|he|מינהל השיכון הפדרלי|simple|Federal Housing Administration|qid=Q474305|lt=Federal Housing Administration}} redevelopment. The shrine was restored from 1968-1969 at a cost of $170,000. Funds were donated entirely by the people of Hawaii. The shrine was rededicated on 22 December 1968.<ref>Miyao, Richard T. Izumo Taishakyo Mission of Hawaii Centennial Anniversary Saga of a Church in Hawaii, 1906-2006. Hawaii Hochi, Ltd. Honolulu, Hawaii. 2006. p. 92.</ref>

{{ill|1885|en|1885|qid=Q7821|lt=1885}} (18th year of Meiji) under the Japan–Hawaii Immigration Treaty was enshrined in {{ill|1906|en|1906|qid=Q2049|lt=1906}} (39th year of Meiji) by {{ill|Japanese in Hawaii|en|Japanese in Hawaii|qid=Q6158764|lt=Japanese immigrants who migrated to Hawaii}}. == History and Tradition ==
* {{ill|1906|en|1906|qid=Q2049|lt=1906}} – A [[:en:Kannushi|Shinto Priest]] from {{ill|Hiroshima Prefecture|en|Hiroshima Prefecture|qid=Q617375|lt=Hiroshima Prefecture}}, {{ill|Miyao Katsuyoshi|ja|宮王勝良|qid=Q140446136}}, was dispatched to Hawaii on the order of the 2nd head of {{ill|Izumo-taishakyo|fa|ایزومو-تایشاکیو|ja|出雲大社教|simple|Izumo-taishakyo|qid=Q6102386|lt=Izumo Taisha Religion}}, {{ill|Sengetakaaki|ja|千家尊愛|qid=Q140446137|lt=Sengetakaaki}}, and began propagating the Izumo faith in the Ala Moana area of Honolulu.
* {{ill|1907|en|1907|qid=Q2048|lt=1907}} – In the downtown area at the triangular intersection of King Street and Beretania Street (Parama area), the precincts were established and the first church hall and shrine were completed.

* {{ill|1922|en|1922|qid=Q2165|lt=1922}} – A new shrine building, modeled after the main shrine, was constructed on the premises. The following year, a grand festival was held to welcome the delegation of the 3rd head of {{ill|Izumo-taishakyo|fa|ایزومو-تایشاکیو|ja|出雲大社教|simple|Izumo-taishakyo|qid=Q6102386|lt=Izumo Taisha Religion}}, {{ill|Sengetakamochi|ja|千家尊有|qid=Q140446138|lt=Sengetakamochi}}, and others.
* {{ill|1935|en|1935|qid=Q18658|lt=1935}} – {{ill|Miyao Katsuyoshi|ja|宮王勝良|qid=Q140446136}} returned to Japan. After obtaining Shinto priest qualifications in the Empire of Japan, his second son, {{ill|Miyao Shigemaru|ja|宮王重丸|qid=Q140446139}}, who had been serving in Hawaii since 1931, assumed the position of the 2nd branch head.
* {{ill|1941|ab|1941|af|1941|als|1941|am|1941 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1941|ar|1941|ary|1941|arz|1941|ast|1941|av|1941 сон|avk|1941|ay|1941|az|1941|azb|۱۹۴۱ (میلادی)|ba|1941 йыл|ban|1941|bar|1941|bat_smg|1941|bcl|1941|be|1941|be_x_old|1941|bg|1941|bh|1941|bjn|1941|bn|১৯৪১|bpy|মারি ১৯৪১|br|1941|bs|1941.|ca|1941|cdo|1941 nièng|ce|1941 шо|ceb|1941|ckb|١٩٤١|co|1941|crh|1941|cs|1941|csb|1941|cv|1941|cy|1941|da|1941|de|1941|diq|1941|dsb|1941|el|1941|eml|1941|eo|1941|es|1941|et|1941|eu|1941|ext|1941|fa|۱۹۴۱|fi|1941|fiu_vro|1941|fo|1941|fr|1941|frp|1941|frr|1941|fur|1941|fy|1941|ga|1941|gag|1941|gan|1941年|gcr|1941|gd|1941|gl|1941|gn|1941|gv|1941|hak|1941-ngièn|he|1941|hi|१९४१|hif|1941|hr|1941.|hsb|1941|ht|1941 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1941|hy|1941|hyw|1941 թուական|ia|1941|id|1941|ilo|1941|inh|1941 шу|io|1941|is|1941|it|1941|ja|1941年|jbo|1941moi|jv|1941|ka|1941|kaa|1941|kbp|1941|kk|1941 жыл|kn|೧೯೪೧|ko|1941년|krc|1941 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1941|ku|1941|kv|1941-ӧд во|kw|1941|la|1941|lb|1941|lez|1941 йис|li|1941|lij|1941|lmo|1941|ln|1941|lt|1941 m.|lv|1941. gads|mai|१९४१|map_bms|1941|mdf|1941|mg|1941|mhr|1941|mi|1941|min|1941|mk|1941|ml|1941|mn|1941 он|mr|इ.स. १९४१|mrj|1941 и|ms|1941|my|၁၉၄၁|myv|1941 ие|mzn|۱۹۴۱|nah|1941|nap|1941|nds|1941|nds_nl|1941|new|ई सं १९४१|nl|1941|nn|1941|no|1941|nrm|1941|nso|1941|oc|1941|olo|1941|or|୧୯୪୧|os|1941-æм аз|pa|1941|pam|1941|pap|1941|pl|1941|pnb|1941|pt|1941|qu|1941|ro|1941|roa_rup|1941|roa_tara|1941|ru|1941 год|rue|1941|sah|1941 сыл|sc|1941|scn|1941|sco|1941|sd|1941ع|se|1941|sh|1941.|shn|1941|si|1941|simple|1941|sk|1941|sl|1941|smn|1941|sq|1941|sr|1941|stq|1941|su|1941|sv|1941|sw|1941|szl|1941|ta|1941|te|1941|tg|Соли 1941|th|พ.ศ. 2484|tk|1941|tl|1941|tly|1941|tpi|1941|tr|1941|tt|1941 ел|ty|1941|udm|1941 ар|ug|1941 - يىلى|uk|1941|ur|1941ء|uz|1941|vec|1941|vi|1941|vls|1941|vo|1941|wa|1941|war|1941|xmf|1941|yi|1941|za|1941 nienz|zea|1941|zh|1941年|zh_classical|一九四一年|zh_min_nan|1941 nî|zh_yue|1941年|qid=Q5231|lt=1941}} – Due to the {{ill|Attack on Pearl Harbor|en|Attack on Pearl Harbor|qid=Q52418|lt=Attack on Pearl Harbor}}, {{ill|Miyao Shigemaru|ja|宮王重丸|qid=Q140446139}}, his family, and branch officials were detained by the {{ill|Federal Bureau of Investigation|en|Federal Bureau of Investigation|qid=Q8333|lt=FBI}}, and were held on the U.S. mainland until the end of the war in 1945. During their detention, the religious group disbanded, and the shrine and other properties were donated to the Honolulu City and County government, being managed by the Parks and Sanitation Departments.
* {{ill|1946|en|1946|qid=Q18610|lt=1946}} – At the end of the previous year, upon his return from detention, {{ill|Miyao Shigemaru|ja|宮王重丸|qid=Q140446139}} renovated a warehouse on Young Street into a shrine building, and resumed activities as a shrine from the New Year.
* {{ill|1952|en|1952|qid=Q5272|lt=1952}} – The Hawaii Izumo Taisha religious group, with {{ill|Miyao Shigemaru|ja|宮王重丸|qid=Q140446139}} as the plaintiff, gathered over 10,000 signatures and submitted a petition to the Honolulu City Council seeking the return of the shrine building. Although the return was unanimously resolved, the Parks Department contested the return, resulting in prolonged disputes.
* {{ill|1961|en|1961|qid=Q3696|lt=1961}} – After six rounds of movements for return, the religious group ultimately prevailed in court, and the shrine building was returned by the Honolulu City and County government.
* {{ill|1968|en|1968|qid=Q2644|lt=1968}} – Following the redevelopment plan for Kukui Street, the shrine building was relocated and restored to its current location, and a relocation festival was held. The following year, under the service of the 5th head of {{ill|Izumo-taishakyo|fa|ایزومو-تایشاکیو|ja|出雲大社教|simple|Izumo-taishakyo|qid=Q6102386|lt=Izumo Taisha Religion}}, {{ill|Sengemichihiko|ja|千家達彦|qid=Q97626080|lt=Sengemichihiko}}, the "Fuwai Izumo Taisha Completion Celebration and Combined Annual Festival" was observed.
* {{ill|1976|en|1976|qid=Q2480|lt=1976}} – In commemoration of the 200th anniversary of the founding of the United States, during a tour in Hawaii, sumo wrestlers of the {{ill|Japan Sumo Association|en|Japan Sumo Association|qid=Q1426308|lt=Japan Sumo Association}} performed a {{ill|Yokozuna|ja|横綱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yokozuna|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1067277}} {{ill|dohyō-iri|ja|土俵入り|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/dohyō-iri|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11423077}} ceremony as an offering.
* {{ill|1990|en|1990|qid=Q2064|lt=1990}} – Beside the {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|qid=Q234731|lt=Torii}} at the front of the shrine, a "Hiroshima Peace Bell" commemorating the sister city relationship between Honolulu and Hiroshima (established in 1960) was installed by the Honolulu City and County government.
* {{ill|1993|en|1993|qid=Q2065|lt=1993}} – {{ill|Miyao Shigemaru|ja|宮王重丸|qid=Q140446139}} returned to Japan. The current leader, Mr. Daiya Amano (天野大也), assumed the position of the 3rd branch head.
* {{ill|2006|en|2006|qid=Q2021|lt=2006}} – Under the service of the 5th head of {{ill|Izumo-taishakyo|fa|ایزومو-تایشاکیو|ja|出雲大社教|simple|Izumo-taishakyo|qid=Q6102386|lt=Izumo Taisha Religion}}, {{ill|Sengemichihiko|ja|千家達彦|qid=Q97626080|lt=Sengemichihiko}}, the "Fuwai Izumo Taisha 100th Anniversary Grand Festival" was held{{sfn|前田孝和|1999|p=149-182}}{{sfn|Miyao, Richard T., ed.|2006|pp=76-93}}.

== Others ==
* The shrine office reception hours are from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM. Due to the closure of the front gate outside these hours, visits for {{ill|Sanpai|ja|参拝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/worship|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11410186}} are not allowed. The area surrounding the shrine is one of the less secure areas even within Honolulu, and visiting after dark is extremely dangerous{{sfn|Hawaii Pacific Press|p=7}}. Prayers and related activities require prior reservation.
* In addition to the principal deity, as guardian deities for immigrants from Okinawa Prefecture, branch spirits from {{ill|Okinawa Shrine|en|Okinawa Shrine|qid=Q11139392|lt=Okinawa Shrine}}, {{ill|Naminoue Shrine|abstract|Q704636|fr|Naminoue-gū|id|Kuil Naminoue|ja|波上宮|zh|波上宮|qid=Q704636|lt=Hagami Shrine}}, and {{ill|Futemma-gū|ja|普天満宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futemmangu Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11514556}} were enshrined in 1941. Branch deities from {{ill|Ebisu Shrine|ja|恵比寿神社}}, {{ill|Inari shrine|fa|معبد ایناری|fr|Sanctuaire Inari|ja|稲荷神社|ko|이나리 신사|simple|Inari shrine|uk|Святилище Інарі|qid=Q514480|lt=Inari Shrine}}, the guardian deity of the Wai'anae area (which was the Kosha of Hawaii Izumo Taisha), and ancestral shrines enshrined throughout [[:en:Oahu|Oʻahu]] were also enshrined{{sfn|IZUMO TAISHA NEWSLETTER|Spring 2012|p=4}}.
* During the New Year, on the {{ill|Three Days|ja|三ヶ日|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Days|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11354062}} period for {{ill|Hatsumōde|ar|هاتسوموده|de|Hatsumōde|es|Hatsumōde|eu|Hatsumōde|fa|هاتسوموده|fr|Hatsumōde|hu|Hacumóde|hy|Հացումոդե|id|Hatsumōde|ja|初詣|jv|Hatsumōde|ko|하쓰모데|my|ဟဆုမိုဒဲ|pl|Hatsumōde|pt|Hatsumōde|ru|Хацумодэ|simple|Hatsumoude|tr|Hatsumōde|zh|初詣|zh_classical|初詣|qid=Q1032381|lt=Hatsumode}}, over 10,000 worshipers, primarily local residents of Hawaii, visit, and not only those of Japanese ancestry but people of various ethnic backgrounds are in attendance{{sfn|Miyao, Richard T., ed.|2006|pp=102-105}}.
* Every year on {{ill|August 6|en|August 6|qid=Q2787|lt=August 6}}, at the "Hiroshima Peace Bell," prayers for world peace are offered in conjunction with religious figures from other religions such as {{ill|Buddhism|en|Buddhism|qid=Q748|lt=Buddhism}}, {{ill|Christianity|en|Christianity|qid=Q5043|lt=Christianity}}, and {{ill|Judaism|en|Judaism|qid=Q9268|lt=Judaism}}.{{sfn|Miyao, Richard T., ed.|2006|pp=111-113}}
